findings.summary: A 2D rotation moves points around a fixed centre point on a plane, preserving distance from that centre. The rotation angle, measured in degrees or radians, defines the turn amount and direction (clockwise or counter-clockwise). Mathematically, the original coordinates are transformed using trigonometric functions: the new x-coordinate equals the original x times the cosine of the angle minus the original y times the sine of the angle, while the new y-coordinate equals the original x times the sine plus the original y times the cosine. This operation can be represented as multiplying a column vector by a rotation matrix or by multiplying a complex number by e^{iθ}. The transformation preserves the point's distance from the centre and the angle between the original and rotated positions equals the rotation angle.

mechanisms.title: Matrix transformation
mechanisms.explanation: The point (x, y) is treated as a column vector and multiplied by a 2×2 matrix containing cosine and sine of the rotation angle. This produces new coordinates (x', y') that represent the rotated position.

mechanisms.title: Complex number multiplication
mechanisms.explanation: Points are represented as complex numbers x + iy. Rotating by angle θ involves multiplying the number by e^{iθ} and expanding using Euler's formula. Equating real and imaginary parts yields the same coordinate transformation as the matrix method.

unknowns: How the rotation matrix entries are precomputed or stored in specific software implementations
Whether the rotation origin is always the coordinate origin or can be any arbitrary point in the plane
If commutative properties observed in complex number rotations hold for all game engine rotation functions
The numerical precision handling when applying repeated small rotations over many frames
